arxiv-2105-12593.title: Exponential Formulas, Normal Ordering and the Weyl–Heisenberg Algebra
arxiv-2105-12593.creator: Stjepan MELJANAC a and Rina ŠTRAJN b
arxiv-2105-12593.description: Abstract We consider a class of exponentials in the Weyl–Heisenberg algebra with exponents of type at most linear in coordinates and arbitrary functions of momenta. They are expressed in terms of normal ordering where coordinates stand to the left from momenta.

The Schwarzschild-de Sitter (SdS) metric is the simplest spacetime solution in general relativity with both a black hole event horizon and a cosmological event horizon. arxiv-2212-04621.title: A systematic literature review on Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality in terms of privacy, authorization and data-leaks
arxiv-2212-04621.creator: Parth D Patel, Prem Trivedi
arxiv-2212-04621.description: Abstract In recent years, VR and AR has exploded into a multimillionaire market. As this emerging technology has spread to a variety of businesses and is rapidly increasing among users. It is critical to address potential privacy and security concerns that these technologies might pose.

arxiv-2308-04966.title: Tidal Response and Shape of Hot Jupiters
arxiv-2308-04966.creator: Sean M. Wahl, Daniel Thorngren, Tiger Lu, Burkhard Militzer
arxiv-2308-04966.description: Abstract We study the response of hot Jupiters to a static tidal perturbation using the Concentric MacLaurin Spheroid (CMS) method. For strongly irradiated planets, we first performed radiative transfer calculations to relate the planet’s equilibrium temperature, T eq T_{\mathrm{eq}} , to its interior entropy.

arxiv-2410-05569.title: The Hypertriton Puzzle in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2410-05569.creator: Thomas Cohen and Maneesha Pradeep University of Maryland, College Park
arxiv-2410-05569.description: Abstract The yields of hadrons and light nuclei in relativistic collisions of heavy-nuclei at a center of mass energy of s N ​ N = 2.6 ​ TeV \sqrt{s_{NN}}\,=\,2.6\,\text{TeV} can be described remarkably well by a thermal distribution of an ideal gas of hadrons and light nuclei interacting only via the decay of resonances.

arxiv-2502-19883.title: Beyond the Tip of Efficiency: Uncovering the Submerged Threats of Jailbreak Attacks in Small Language Models
arxiv-2502-19883.creator: Sibo Yi 1 Tianshuo Cong 1,4 Xinlei He 3 Qi Li 1,2 Jiaxing Song 1,2 1 Tsinghua University 2 Zhongguancun Laboratory 3 The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) 4 Shandong Key Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence Security ysb23@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn , xinleihe@hkust-gz.edu.cn , {
arxiv-2502-19883.description: Abstract Small language models (SLMs) have become increasingly prominent in the deployment on edge devices due to their high efficiency and low computational cost. While researchers continue to advance the capabilities of SLMs through innovative training strategies and model compression techniques, the security risks of SLMs have received considerably less attention compared to large language models (LLMs).

arxiv-2505-07450.title: Prototype Augmented Hypernetworks for Continual Learning
arxiv-2505-07450.creator: Neil De La Fuente, Maria Pilligua, Daniel Vidal, Albin Soutiff, Cecilia Curreli, Daniel Cremers, Andrey Barsky, [1.5mm] Computer Vision Center
arxiv-2505-07450.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Neil De La Fuente, Maria Pilligua, Daniel Vidal, Albin Soutiff, Cecilia Curreli, Daniel Cremers, Andrey Barsky, [1.5mm] Computer Vision Center. Continual learning (CL) aims to learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting prior knowledge, but gradient updates for a new task often overwrite the weights learned earlier, causing catastrophic forgetting (CF). We propose Prototype-Augmented Hypernetworks ( P ​ A ​ H PAH ), a framework where a single hypernetwork, conditioned on learnable task prototypes, dynamically generates task-specific classifier heads on demand.

arxiv-2507-11770.title: Generating Actionable Robot Knowledge Bases by Combining 3D Scene Graphs with Robot Ontologies
arxiv-2507-11770.creator: Giang Nguyen, Mihai Pomarlan, Sascha Jongebloed, Nils Leusmann, Minh Nhat Vu, Michael Beetz
arxiv-2507-11770.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giang Nguyen, Mihai Pomarlan, Sascha Jongebloed, Nils Leusmann, Minh Nhat Vu, Michael Beetz. In robotics, the effective integration of environmental data into actionable knowledge remains a significant challenge due to the variety and incompatibility of data formats commonly used in scene descriptions, such as MJCF, URDF, and SDF. This paper presents a novel approach that addresses these challenges by developing a unified scene graph model that standardizes these varied formats into the Universal Scene Description (USD) format.

arxiv-2509-13190.creator: Yuval Roichman
arxiv-2509-13190.description: Abstract . A recent result of Cohen and Zemel provides an elegant expansion of the Rasala polynomials for symmetric group character degrees. In this note we present an alternative short algebraic proof. Extensions to polynomials of character values follow. 1. arxiv-2511-12455.title: Generative Reconstruction of Spatiotemporal Wall-Pressure in Turbulent Boundary Layers via Patchwise Latent Diffusion Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2511-12455.creator: Xiantao Fan, Meet Hemant Parikh, Yi Liu, Xin-Yang Liu, Junyi Guo, Meng Wang, Jian-Xun Wang
arxiv-2511-12455.description: Abstract Wall-pressure fluctuations in turbulent boundary layers drive flow-induced noise, structural vibration, and hydroacoustic disturbances, especially in underwater and aerospace systems. Accurate prediction of their wavenumber-frequency spectra is critical for mitigation and design, yet empirical/analytical models rely on simplifying assumptions and miss the full spatiotemporal complexity, while high-fidelity simulations are prohibitive at high Reynolds numbers.

pmc-10564115.title: Cost Analysis of High-Flow Oxygen Therapy Compared with Conventional Oxygen Therapy in Severe COVID-19 in Colombia: Data from a Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-10564115.creator: Sergio I Prada, Maria P Garcia-Garcia, Gustavo A Ospina-Tascón, Diego Rosselli
pmc-10564115.description: BackgroundA randomized clinical trial (HiFlo-COVID-19 Trial) showed that among patients with severe COVID-19, treatment with high-flow oxygen therapy (HFOT) significantly reduced the need for invasive mechanical ventilation support and time for clinical recovery compared with conventional oxygen therapy (COT). However, the cost of this strategy is unknown.ObjectiveWe examined total cost of HFOT treatment compared with COT in real-world setting.

pmc-10671707.title: Identification of a Male-Produced Aggregation Sex Pheromone in Rosalia batesi, an Endemic Japanese Longhorn Beetle
pmc-10671707.creator: Midori Fukaya, Satoshi Kiriyama, Saki Yagami, Ryûtarô Iwata, Hiroe Yasui, Masahiko Tokoro, Yunfan Zou, Jocelyn G Millar, Jean-François Picimbon
pmc-10671707.description: Simple SummaryRosalia batesi Harold (Cerambycidae) is a longhorned beetle endemic to Japan distributed on the mainland from Hokkaido (north) to Kyushu (south). The beautiful appearance of the adults is renowned not only in Japan but worldwide. The larvae feed in the trunks of broad-leaf trees.

pmc-10674418.title: The FDA’s New Guideline “Generally Accepted Scientific Knowledge” (GASK): An Opportunity to Expedite the Approval of Biosimilars
pmc-10674418.creator: Sarfaraz K Niazi, Giorgio Cozza
pmc-10674418.description: The US FDA’s new guideline suggests using “Generally Accepted Science Knowledge” (GASK) to develop nonclinical testing protocols for developing drugs and biologicals to remove unnecessary testing. Interpreting acceptable scientific knowledge as a rational approach has motivated the author to suggest substantial changes to the development of biosimilars, as demonstrated in this paper.

pmc-11470996.description: nd its subjournals. pmc-11541775.title: Reversal of tyrosine-linked ADP-ribosylation by ARH3 and PARG
pmc-11541775.creator: Johannes Gregor Matthias Rack, Jim Voorneveld, Edoardo José Longarini, Sven Wijngaarden, Kang Zhu, Alessandra Peters, Jia Jhing Sia, Evgeniia Prokhorova, Dragana Ahel, Ivan Matić, Dmitri V. Filippov, Ivan Ahel
pmc-11541775.description: ADP-ribosylation is an ancient posttranslational modification with exceptional versatility in terms of breadth of modification targets including at least seven different amino acid side chains, various moieties on nucleic acids, and a variety of small chemical compounds. The spatiotemporal signaling dynamic of the different modification variations is tightly regulated and depends on the writers, erases, and readers of each type.

pmc-12410360.title: Nanotechnology strategies for endometrium health: Are we on the right track?
pmc-12410360.creator: Victoria Herrara, Dana Tarab-Ravski, Subhash C. Chauhan, Nikesh Narang, Mohammad Mirazul Islam, Dan Peer, Rajendra Prasad, Murali M. Yallapu
pmc-12410360.description: The endometrium is a vital mucosal tissue which undergoes cyclical regeneration, differentiation, and remodeling upon hormonal, cellular, and molecular signaling networks. Dysregulation of these processes can trigger a range of pathological conditions including chronic inflammatory disorders, hyperplastic lesions, malignancies, and infertility, necessitating the need for effective therapeutic interventions.

pmc-12766092.title: Multifunctional signal probe-based immunochromatographic test strip for rapid detection of aflatoxin B1 in complex matrix samples
pmc-12766092.creator: Wenjie Ren, Ting Wang, Jiarui Pang, Yifan Li, Yuxiu Han, Baoshan He, Renyong Zhao, Min Wei, Wenhong Zhao, Zhiguang Suo, Yiwei Xu, Zhui Tu
pmc-12766092.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Immunochromatographic test strips (ICTS) are widely used for the immediate and rapid detection of toxins; however, they are prone to false-positive results and insufficient sensitivity when applied to complex sample matrices. To overcome these limitations, herein, a multifunctional signal probe-based ICTS was developed for the rapid detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) in complex matrix samples by conjugating biotinylated nanobodies (G8-Bio) with streptavidin-modified magnetic beads (MB-SA) as the probes. The constructed ICTS achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.063 ng/mL for AFB1.

pmc-13006308.title: Geospatial optimization of Air-Mobile Stroke Unit deployment in Norway: expanding the frontiers of neurocritical care
pmc-13006308.creator: Caroline J. Jagtenberg, Annemijn M. Boer, Marius Rehn, Jo Roislien, Maren R. Hov, Karianne Larsen
pmc-13006308.description: IntroductionRural and remote communities face disadvantages in acute stroke care. An Air-Mobile Stroke Unit (Air-MSU), adapting traditional MSUs for aircraft, could enable timely prehospital assessment in underserved regions. This modeling study aimed to identify the optimal Air-MSU base in Norway to maximize patient coverage, using increased geographic reach within 4.5 h as a proxy for clinical efficacy and improved outcomes.

pmc-13016891.creator: Daisuke Fujisawa, Eisho Yoshikawa, Maiko Fujimori, Sachiko Arai, Makoto Kobayakawa, Akiko Kurata, Ayako Kayano, Kanako Ichikura, Yuri Igarashi, Hiroyuki Otani, Yuko Yanai, Tomoko Baba, Yoshiro Okajima, Akiko Abe, Yu Uneno, Masako Okamura, Yoshihisa Matsumoto, Kurumi Asaumi, Kazuho Hisamura, Kanae Mo

As Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Escherichia coli continue to evolve rapidly, it is critical to develop novel therapeutic agents and structurally unique antibacterial medicines.

pmc-13215953.title: A semi-replicating VSV (srVSV)-based platform for developing broad-spectrum mucosal vaccines against influenza A viruses
pmc-13215953.creator: Xianmiao Ye, Junnan Lu, Zirong Han, Zhishan Fan, Xinru Hu, Lichuang Jiao, Lisha Deng, Wenming Liu, Junqi Liu, Weiqi Pan, Ling Chen, Liqiang Feng, Caijun Sun
pmc-13215953.description: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are significant respiratory pathogens characterized by high mutation rates and frequent genetic reassortments, underscoring the need for vaccines that can induce robust and broadly protective mucosal immunity. While replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) vectors have the potential to elicit mucosal immunity, their neurovirulence raises significant safety concerns.

pmc-13563988.title: Immune Modulation and Evasion by Cryptococcus spp.: An Integrative Review of Molecular Mechanisms and Experimental Evidence
pmc-13563988.creator: Yohana Porto Calegari-Alves, Luana Carolina Cardozo, Walter Orlando Beys-da-Silva, Lucélia Santi
pmc-13563988.description: The Cryptococcus species complex are major human pathogenic fungi capable of causing cryptococcosis, a severe pneumonia and meningitidis in both immunocompromised and, in some cases, immunocompetent patients. Their pathogenic success depends not only on classical virulence factors, but also on a coordinated capacity to evade, modulate, and exploit host immune responses across multiple stages of infection.
